Subject: Re: RC26-0205 - Great House Farm, Williams/ Buckler Family, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan
From: Sion Buckler
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 22:56 UTC
------------------------------------------------------------

Thanks Adam.

Having recently completed my 2022 years in Oath as a public servant.
Employed under the welsh government/ Vale of Glamorgan for the last 2 of
it. And left my military career with honours before that. I always prided
myself serving as a public servant.

But I am outraged at what occured to my family and its a huge scandal. And
anyone in office should not be treating this like an us/them situation
where I'm going up against my Welsh Govenrment and fudiciaries.

There's a lot of women in my family too terrified to even speak up against
this. My father alledged fraud. He died. My grandad died before being able
to explain how BP got our title. My nan died in the window she had to
challenge BP's registration of our land in their names. I am the only one
who is willing to speak up and out about this.

Its not I wasn't frightened like they were. Its that statute of limitation
applied and there wasn't much that could be done. But I suspect fraud as of
this year and this means this can and should be reopened.

I am horrified that the MP and Councillor for Llandough are remaining
silent. Not responding. But its possible they might need time to take a
position on this. So far as I see the British (Thatcher and BP) seem
implicated. And us indigenous welsh on our ancestral birthland home since
1667, makes this very bad for them.

So if there's any Welsh still in Wales, that care that our herritage and
history could be looted and history covered up as this appears to have, I
hope someone else will make noise about this too. And not just let it rest.

Marconi stayed with us while inventing radio and there's not even a plaque
to commemorate Church View Close, Llandough as the birthplace of radio.
This is a huge scandal. I understand many Brits are liberal left and
Marconi was right wing. Thats what Cardiff City Council say about why
there's no plaque to commemorate marconi on the statute of a radio at
Cardiff Bay. But this perversion and supression of history and facts is so
unacceptable. I have nephews and children and the fact they can't see any
trace of our 320 years in Llandough , up until 1988 is an outrage. The fact
the press all labelled us squatters and thats what they will grow up
reading, when it was our home since 1667 is also an outrage. They're
clearly hostages under terrorists and there's nothing democratic about any
of this.

So far as I see what happened to our family in 1988 , in how we were
displaced, isn't just tyranny or british colonising. It's a literally act
of terrorism. Which I reported to police yesterday as such. And I consider
my family there in Wales hostages under said terrorists. The situation is
untenable. We require remedy. Narrative justice. Correction of records.
Some press release. Something to amend this situation.

The fact ITV quietly just declassified footage from 1988 after 38 years was
cowardly. They cannot expect to get away with that.  The footage clearly
says neighbours report SAS used and the footage shows SAS and there's
mention of the land being prime Real Estate overlooking cardiff bay. But
more so is the fact that my old best friends late mum, Nichola Hayward
Thomas, who is the news anchor, never mentioned this footage to me and took
this to her grave. And in the clip she fails to mention the assault on my
mum, while serving the injuction to the illegal occupiers terrorists,
properly SAS. Didn't just dislocate her shoulder. But she was pregnant with
three toddlers. So even the declassified footage after 38 years supressed,
is itself carefully scripted to show bias. And there's more on that. Like
the fact the edit/ cut is so abrupt when the SAS looking man or mention of
real estate value being prime.

We scattered to the wind, looted and half dead in 1988 after decades of
lawfare and this terrorist attack and siege on our home. We want justice.
Because what we've said all along seems to have been the plausible story.
And what the press, records and courts ruled seems to be the fraud.

Without legitimacy there's no authority here. It's important as fudiciaries
you be legitimate.

I'm horrified at the replies I have received thus far. Like CADW saying
they had nothing to do with this or land registry converting my query into
a complaint only to squash is. And failing that some other cowardly reply.

There's institutional failure. There's court mistakes. Theres proceedural
unfairness.
Purgergy and fraud. I expect better from the Welsh Govenrment to fix this.

Please do everything in your power.
This is all I ask.

Regards,

Sion Buckler
[address redacted], Dinas Powys, Vale of Glamorgan

>
>
>
> Thank you for your enquiry. As noted in my email of 26 November last,
> while we cannot advise you on a legal case or undertake a review of
> historical decisions, we do hold information and archives related to Great
> House Farm, Llandough.
>
>
>
> The site entry and description for the site in the National Monuments
> Record of Wales can be seen online on Coflein, here:
> https://coflein.gov.uk/en/site/20182.
>
>
>
> We hold 14 archives related to the site, a list of which can be seen here:

> be viewed in our Search Room, located in the National Library of Wales,
> which is open Tuesday through Thursday, 9:30-16:30. If you would like to
> view the material in person, I would advise arranging with us beforehand so
> that we can prepare the material ahead of your visit. Some of the material
> is on microfiche and as we do not have a microfiche reader in the Search
> Room, we will need to liaise with the National Library Reading Room staff
> to try to negotiate the use of their machines ahead of your visit. However,
> I have located an electronic copy of Archive Number 6524751, which can be
> accessed here:
> https://www.walesher1974.org/her/app/php/herumd.php?group=GGAT&level=3&docid=301361628
>
>
>
> While it is possible to order scans of material using the attached order
> form, we may be unable to provide research-quality scans or photographs of
> some of the material, such as the material on microfiche, which would
> require high-resolution scanning at a cost of £20 per scan. Moreover,  many
> of these records remain under third-party copyright, and we would only be
> able to provide scans or copies for personal, non-commercial research.
> Other uses, such as use in a legal case or report would likely require the
> permission of the copyright holder(s). I would therefore advise arranging
> to view the material in person rather than ordering scans, if possible.
>
>
>
> Finally, I have confirmed with our Records Manager that we do not hold any

>
>
>
> Thank you again for your enquiry.

>
>
> Sincerely,
>
>
>

>
> Sir / Madam,
>
> To all those whom it concerns, BCC'd into this email.
>
> I write to request disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act 2000
> and, where applicable, the Environmental Information Regulations 2004.
>
> This request concerns Great House Farm / Ty Mawr (Great House), Llandough,
> associated estate lands, historic occupation and related heritage records.
> My family is Buckler and before that Williams, and we occupied Great House
> Farm from 1667 until our forceful dispossession of it in 1988.  Without our
> ownership ever having been estiguished and without BP ever having a ruling
> of ownership, only possession.
>
> It's alledged our fee simple absolute and manorial title was stolen. And
> when BP registered our lands in their names in 1982, with our stolen title,
> my nan who challenged this all her life, during the 2 week land registry
> window to challenge BP's registration, which they achieved via purgergy and
> document/ identity fraud, she conveniently died. As my father did after his
> appeal of the 1987 mistake ruling was mistakely dismissed and his ECHR
> request blocked and home abruptly demolished, which he was prevented from
> stopping having been hospitalised and arrested without charges by armed
> force officers and possible SAS.
>
> https://youtu.be/0eXOoj7eUCo?si=hcgSA2pFgEE943HG
>
> I understand records may exist within the National Monuments Record of
> Wales, Historic Environment Record archives, archaeological consultations
> and planning files, including references already identified as:
>
> • Great House Farm HER site entry – GGAT03586s
> • Land at Great House Farm HER event entry – GGATE003872
> • The 1990 archaeological assessment commissioned by BP Properties Ltd.
>
> Please provide copies of, or access to:
>
>    1. All records concerning Great House Farm / Ty Mawr / Great House
>    Estate, Llandough including:
>
> • surveys
> • reports
> • site notes
> • photographs
> • maps
> • aerial imagery
> • GIS layers
> • archive material
> • annotations
> • title references
> • occupancy references
> • landscape records
> • archaeological observations.
>
>    2. All internal and external correspondence involving:
>
> • RCAHMW / NMRW
> • Cadw
> • GGAT / Heneb
> • Vale of Glamorgan Council
> • BP Properties Ltd
> • developers
> • planning authorities
> • landowners, estate representatives or consultants.
>
>    3. Any documents discussing:
>
> • estate ownership
> • occupation history
> • family occupation or association
> • agricultural use
> • commemorative tree planting or memorial planting
> • estate boundaries
> • title history
> • acquisition history
> • disputes concerning ownership, heritage status or land use
> • estate restructuring, extinguishment, compulsory acquisition or title
> alteration.
>
>    4. Copies of all material linked to GGAT03586s and GGATE003872,
>    including the archaeological assessment and associated correspondence.
>    5. Any records identifying historic occupants, proprietors, tenants or
>    family associations, including references to the Williams family where
>    present within archives.
>    6. Metadata identifying file creators, accession history, provenance,
>    dates and retention schedules.
>    7. File indexes, archive references or schedules identifying further
>    related material not already listed.
>
> Please provide information electronically where possible.
>
> If any material is withheld, please identify the exemption relied upon and
> provide the public interest assessment.
>
> Regards,
>
>
>
> Sion Buckler
>
> [address redacted], Dinas Powys
> [map link redacted]

Subject: Re: RC26-0205 - Great House Farm, Williams/ Buckler Family, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan - Further Details of Archives
From: Sion Buckler
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 19:38 UTC
------------------------------------------------------------

Adam,

Thanks.

I'm at the Welsh Settlement in Patagonia to reconstruct a replica of our
former 10 bed court house/manor house. If I haven't said already. I will
try to respond to this, but forgive me in advance as my times limited am
I'm sure yours is. And this is deeply traumatic. I am still the only one in
my family half able and willing to speak up and out about this.

My grandmother was only Mrs Buckler for a short time, from her marriage in
1935 until she changed her name back to Mrs Williams, as I understand — if
she was ever Mrs Buckler at all. Since her Williams name and "Williams
Title" (as the courts cite) were important to her ancestral and hereditary
land claim. Whereas the dead legal name Mrs Buckler, with no such rights as
the indigenous living woman on her ancestral birthland, did have rights.
And the courts' and BP's and land registries' use of Mrs Buckler as her
name, long after it ceased to exist, I believe is at least a mistake.
Considering it falls within the context of a campaign to dispossess this
disabled widow's pension and us of our family home and land since 1667, I
would say that mistake and distinction ought to be corrected on the public
record. I would like to know the procedure where it concerns your
department. Or if a note can be made of this on the files where the mistake
exists. If it exists. I will be happy to provide her death certificate as
Mrs Williams and so forth, if helpful.

The other matter is the fact of the 1975 and 1983 conveyance of two titles
and merging of two titles. Both were treated as the surrounding farmland
and leased and defaulted on the lease of the surrounding farmland. But if
it were indeed the case that Mrs Williams had absolute title of her
farmhouse and garden, aside from the 999-year lease of surrounding farmland
acquired in 1667, then the above conveyances show that her land and home
were unlawfully absorbed into the land BP acquired and gained possession
of, treating her home and garden as one and the same when they were not.
Ownership was never ruled on. BP sought possession and never gained a
ruling on ownership.

So Mrs Williams and our family's home and garden and ownership claim and
plot appears to not have been extinguished, but instead possession of our
home and garden appears to have been taken by force — possibly military
too, not just police — as if our home and garden were subject to the
possession of the surrounding farmland. Confusion caused may stem from BP
withholding the fact Mary was challenging their claim of ownership of her
land and garden from the land registry in 1983.

Mary conveniently died the fortnight she had to challenge BP merging her
title into theirs. The land registry also appears to have used the invalid
Mrs Buckler name from her 1935 marriage, disregarding the name change
reversion, to validate the name Mrs Buckler on BP's licence letters offered
in 1974. To which were allegedly not rejected despite Mary going to the
papers to expressly reject as per the 1974 article and expressly rejected
access in 1975 during the conveyance. The land registry also would have had
to depend on the 1974 quashed and earlier adjourned court documents to
corroborate BP's filings, but allege to have not seen or known the land was
disputed by Mary Williams and my family, while depending on court documents
explicitly detailing that Mary Williams and my family were challenging BP.
The 1974 licence letters, wrongly validated retrospectively in 1987, as did
the land registry try to validate their actions in 1983 using a ruling 4
years later as their defence. BP lost in 1974. The challenge of ownership
could not be ruled on in their favour nor ruled against in Mary's. Nor did
they win possession. The press sided with Mary. The courts to an extent
too, saying she couldn't present title, which isn't to say it didn't exist.
And we won in the hearts and minds of the 1100+ people who petitioned BP in
1974. Their licence letters afterwards, after my nan conveniently didn't
get her audience and ruling in her favour with the court for the second
time that year due to adjourning and squashing, appear to have been
backdated. And lacked validity due to the 1975 conveyance where BP
themselves clearly did not leave Mary alone as their own licence terms.
Notwithstanding the name was wrong on them. Notwithstanding Mary did
explicitly reject them publicly and in the 1975 conveyance.

A series of institutional failures and court mistakes and procedural
unfairness and fraud appears to have occurred, notwithstanding the
convenient timed death of my grandmother in the 2-week window to challenge
BP's registering of our home and garden and land in their names in 1983. Or
the convenient death of my father after his appeal of the 1987 ruling was
dismissed and his ECHR blocked and his property abruptly destroyed. ITV
failing to report that 24 hours before that abrupt demolition us 3 children
and pregnant mum were inside. ITV footage suppressed until late last year
along with much other media, still suppressed.

I don't say all this to offload the trauma of it all onto you. I say all
this to say that I am still a constituent of this community and my family
had standing in this community and county since 1667 and still do with our
current house we have in the neighbouring town, since the 50's. Which my
grandad Ray Smith purchased after starring in Exodus with Paul Newman. And
for 38 years we have, all of us, been utterly deceived by headlines saying
we were squatters being evicted. Or like in 1987 the judge said Mary
Williams "conceived the notion she owned". Her paper title was stolen from
her so far as I understand in my research so far. She still appears to have
defeated the attempts to dispossess our family of our home in the early to
later half of the 1900's due to a copy of the paper in the public library.
Which in later cases could not be presented as that went missing too. Which
in later court cases, despite paper title not being able to be presented,
still did not defeat or extinguish our ownership claim due to our long
standing. And to this day our ownership claim has not been lawfully or
legally extinguished or surrendered or transferred or sold by the inheritor
of the Williams Title i.e. Mrs Williams, or her heirs or successors i.e. my
late father and now my cousins, 5 aunties, tens of cousins, and brothers
and sisters.

Our family is now a small army. And all of this information is surfacing

   - Ownership and occupation of the farmhouse and garden were actively
   contested in 1974, with a defence asserting adverse possession filed on
   behalf of Mary Williams, and the matter adjourned without a final
   determination of title.
   - Enforcement of earlier possession orders was deferred, a warrant was
   withdrawn on 31 October 1974, and the occupier remained in possession until
   her death in 1983.
   - Despite this, land registration, demolition (1988), and archaeological
   intervention proceeded without a High Court determination of ownership and
   without disclosure of earlier, locally known archaeological discoveries.
   - A Roman burial reportedly discovered beneath the farmhouse in 1888 by
   the occupying family appears not to have been reflected in later “rescue”
   excavations (1978–1980) or the major 1994 excavation, which treated Roman
   and early medieval burials as newly revealed.

Taken together, this produces an archival landscape in which:

   - court files relating to decisive events appear absent or incomplete;
   - later records imply finality where proceedings were in fact unresolved;
   - and the destruction of a long-occupied medieval structure occurred
   before the site’s known archaeological significance was formally
   acknowledged.

I note and appreciate your confirmation that the principal judicial series
(J 157, J 83, J 84) contain no relevant material. Given the scale of the
consequences flowing from the dispute—forced removal, demolition of an
occupied dwelling, and loss of heritage fabric—the absence of supporting
court or administrative files is itself significant for researchers.

Accordingly, I would be grateful for guidance on the following procedural
points:

   - how researchers are expected to interpret gaps or silence in the
   archival record where substantial actions plainly occurred;
   - whether related non-judicial records (for example, departmental,
   planning, regulatory, or corporate records connected to land registration,
   planning consent, or archaeological works) are more likely to sit outside
   the obvious court series; and
   - whether there is an appropriate mechanism for flagging concerns about
   record completeness or contextual risk, without seeking alteration of the
   records themselves.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am not alleging impropriety on the part of
The National Archives or its staff. My concern is to ensure that the
historical record is approached with appropriate caution where absence may
unintentionally convey certainty or closure that did not exist at the time.

Thank you again for your time and professionalism.

Yours sincerely,

Sion Buckler

   BP/Western Ground Rents acquisition records that are not reflected in the
   current online catalogue?

The 1994 archaeological excavation report (Cotswold Archaeological Trust)

land transaction records from the same period is itself an anomaly
requiring explanation.

You note that parties are generally responsible for maintaining their own
records. However, BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust Ltd were corporate
entities with statutory filing obligations. I ask:

   - Were any BP corporate records relating to land acquisition in South
   Glamorgan (1969-1988) selected for preservation under the Companies Act
   or as part of the public record?
   - Has The National Archives ever received or sought records from BP
   regarding the Great House Farm acquisition, demolition, or the 1987
   litigation?

The Court of Appeal judgment [1987] EWCA Civ 2 notes that BP issued letters
on 31 October 1974, not received until November 4th 1974 —letters that were
allegedly "accepted by silence." The original correspondence would

within 20 working days. Should The National Archives be unable to assist
further, I request a formal referral to the appropriate body with
jurisdiction over historical record fraud and spoliation.

Subject: Re: Subject: Stage Two Complaint – Title WA231076 – Alleged Mistake in the Register
From: Sion Buckler
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 16:10 UTC
------------------------------------------------------------

Dear Sir/Madam,

I write to append further evidence and clarification to my ongoing
complaint regarding the registration of title relating to Great House Farm,
Llandough (also known as Ty Mawr / Great House).

https://youtu.be/4GXmR7mAas0?feature=shared

This submission sets out a series of facts which I can evidence and which,
taken together, raise serious concerns of fraud, concealment, and wrongful
registration that have materially affected the rights of the Williams
family and their heirs.

1. Unauthorised transfer of title (circa 1965)
I can evidence that the title to the property was transferred or sold in or
around 1965 by Frederick Buckler without the knowledge or consent of Mrs
Mary Williams, who maintained a rightful claim to the property. This raises
the issue that the disposition may have been made without lawful authority.

2. Death of key party and concealment (1968)
Frederick Buckler died in 1968. Any knowledge he held regarding the
circumstances of the transfer died with him, preventing proper scrutiny or
challenge at the time.

3. Inability to prove ownership in court (1974)
Mrs Mary Williams was subsequently unable to prove her claim in court
proceedings in 1974. This inability must be viewed in the context of the
prior undisclosed transfer and the absence of key evidence and testimony.

4. Knowledge of defective title by acquiring party
There is a credible basis to assert that the acquiring party (BP and/or its
associated property entities) knew, or ought reasonably to have known, that
the title they acquired was defective. This point is central and I am
compiling supporting material demonstrating notice and/or constructive
knowledge.

5. Registration following death of claimant
Mrs Mary Williams died prior to the land being formally registered in the
name of the acquiring party. As a result, she was denied any opportunity to
rebut, challenge, or correct the position before registration was effected.

6. Death of additional disputing party
Mr Buckler also died during the period in which he was engaged in disputing
the matter. The cumulative effect is that all primary individuals with
direct knowledge were deceased before the issue could be fully and fairly
resolved.

7. Ongoing family claim
Despite these events, the claim of the Williams family has never been
relinquished. The position remains that the title was wrongfully
transferred and subsequently registered on the basis of that defective
transfer.

---

Request for Action

In light of the above, I respectfully request that:

1. This evidence be formally appended to my existing complaint file.
2. The register be reviewed in accordance with provisions relating to
fraud, mistake, and/or rectification.
3. Consideration be given to whether the registration was obtained through
or affected by fraud or concealment.
4. I be informed of the appropriate process for seeking rectification
and/or indemnity.

I am prepared to provide supporting documents, including historical
records, press reports, and family documentation, upon request or via
secure submission.

Given the seriousness of the matters raised, I would be grateful for
written confirmation that this submission has been received and attached to
my complaint, along with an outline of the next steps.

Yours faithfully,


Sion Buckler

On Sun, 19 Apr 2026, 16:29 Sion Buckler, <[email redacted]> wrote:

>  Sir or Madam,
>
> I write to ask that my complaint regarding title number WA231076 (Land on
> the North Side of Leckwith Road, Llandough) be escalated to **stage two**
> of HM Land Registry’s Complaints Procedure. This email sets out why I
> consider the stage‑one decision to be incorrect, identifies the mistake I
> say exists in the register, and explains the decision I seek.
>
> ### 1. My core contention
>
> My core contention is that BP Properties Limited were registered as
> proprietors on the basis of a factual and legal error regarding my
> grandmother’s status on the land. My grandmother did not occupy under any
> genuine licence granted to her and did not relinquish any claim. Instead,
> any licence relied on by BP related to a different name/person. As her
> heir, I have succeeded to her claim; I therefore say that registering BP as
> proprietors was a “mistake in the register” for the purposes of the Land
> Registration Act 2002.
>
> ### 2. Identity mismatch and alleged “licence”
>
> Your stage‑one letter records that HM Land Registry relies on the Court of
> Appeal decision in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler  EWCA Civ 2, and treats my
> grandmother as having occupied under a licence granted by the documentary
> title holder, so that her possession was no longer adverse.
>
> However, the alleged licence and related correspondence did not use my
> grandmother’s true legal name. My grandmother was Mrs Williams (supported
> by her birth, marriage and death certificates), not “Mrs Buckler”. The
> “licensee” referred to in BP’s narrative and in the 1987 litigation is
> therefore not the same legal person as my grandmother. There is, in other
> words, a fundamental mis‑identification or identity fraud at the heart of
> the story that HM Land Registry and the Court have relied upon.
>
> If the licence relied on by BP was addressed to, or granted in respect of,
> a different named individual, it cannot properly be said that my
> grandmother’s occupation was under that licence. In that case her
> occupation remained adverse to BP’s paper title, and any finding that she
> was a “licensee” rests on a factual premise that is demonstrably wrong.
>
> ### 3. Timing – “cart before the horse”
>
> Your letter explains that the applications for first registration of
> WA231076 (and the related title WA240304) were made in 1982–83 and that BP
> demonstrated a documentary root of title back to 1969/1975 by way of
> conveyances and a 1971 abstract of title.
>
> You also confirm that the Court of Appeal only gave its decision in BP
> Properties Ltd v Buckler in 1987, holding that an offer by BP to let my
> grandmother remain created a licence and brought her adverse possession to
> an end.
>
> This highlights a fundamental sequencing problem:
>
> - At the date of first registration (1982–83), whether there was a valid
> licence capable of defeating my grandmother’s adverse possession was a
> live, unresolved dispute.
> - BP nevertheless presented themselves as entitled to be registered as
> proprietors and their solicitors certified on form FR1 that there was no
> question or doubt affecting the title.
>
> - HM Land Registry, relying on that certification, registered BP before
> any court had determined whether my grandmother’s possession had
> extinguished BP’s title.
> - Only in 1987 did the Court of Appeal retrospectively treat the alleged
> licence as bringing adverse possession to an end, and that decision was
> itself based on the mis‑identification described above.
>
> In simple terms, the effect of the alleged licence (if any) was judicially
> determined **after** first registration, and on the basis of the wrong
> person being treated as the “licensee”. BP and their solicitors put the
> cart before the horse, and HM Land Registry accepted that position.
>
> ### 4. The specific “mistake in the register”
>
> Your stage‑one response concludes that there is “no evidence of a mistake
> in the register” and therefore no power to alter the register and no right
> to indemnity. I say this is incorrect.
>
> The mistake I allege is as follows:
>
> 1. On the true facts, my grandmother’s occupation of the land was adverse
> to BP’s documentary title and was not under any valid licence granted to
> her.
>
> 2. Her adverse possession had, or may have, extinguished BP’s title by the
> time of first registration in 1982–83, meaning BP were not entitled to be
> registered as proprietors at that time.
>
> 3. HM Land Registry nevertheless registered BP as proprietors on the basis
> of:
>    - a licence attributed to the wrong person (identity error/fraud), and
>    - a solicitor’s FR1 certificate stating there was no question or doubt
> affecting title, despite a long‑running dispute and pending litigation.
>
> 4. Subsequent reliance on the 1987 Court of Appeal decision does not cure
> this, because that decision itself proceeded on the mis‑identification of
> my grandmother and did not and could not retrospectively validate a licence
> that never related to her.
>
> On that analysis, the register shows BP as proprietors when, in law, my
> grandmother’s adverse possession should have extinguished BP’s title and
> given rise to a transmissible proprietary interest which I, as her heir,
> now claim. The register therefore does not accurately reflect the true
> legal position and contains a mistake capable of rectification.
>
> ### 5. Why the stage‑one reasoning is inadequate
>
> In your stage‑one letter you state that:
>
> - HM Land Registry has an administrative function and cannot “look behind
> or challenge decisions of the Court”. [1]
> - My identity‑fraud claims are “not relevant to the issue of title to the
> land” because they relate to the dispute heard by the Court.
>
> - There is no evidence of negligence or maladministration and no evidence
> of a mistake in the register.
>
> With respect, this reasoning is incomplete:
>
> - Once HM Land Registry is presented with clear evidence that the person
> named as the “licensee” in the litigation and licence documentation is not
> the same legal person as the occupier (my grandmother), that goes directly
> to whether the Court of Appeal’s factual premise remains reliable and
> whether the register is accurate.
>
> - Recognising that there is a serious question as to the correctness of
> the register is not the same as “overturning” the Court of Appeal. HM Land
> Registry has statutory powers to alter the register where there is a
> mistake, and it can, where appropriate, refer disputes about rectification
> to the tribunal or the courts.
>
> - To simply say that identity‑fraud concerns are “not relevant to title”
> is, I say, an error of law and/or an unreasonable application of policy. It
> disregards new evidence going to the foundation of BP’s claimed entitlement.
>
> ### 6. The decision and outcome I seek
>
> For stage two, I ask that a Land Registrar (Senior Officer) reconsider the
> complaint and:
>
> 1. Accept that the combination of:
>    - the identity mismatch (licence/name vs my grandmother’s true legal
> name), and
>    - the timing (registration in 1982–83 before the 1987 decision) gives
> rise to at least a **serious question** as to whether the register is
> mistaken in showing BP/ Companies thereafter, as proprietors.
>
> 2. Treat this as evidence of a potential “mistake in the register” for the
> purposes of your alteration powers and Schedule 8, rather than as a mere
> disagreement with the 1987 judgment.
>
> 3. Either:
>
>    - (a) commence the process of rectification, recognising that my
> grandmother’s adverse possession may have extinguished BP’s title and that
> I, as her heir, now have a claim to be registered, or
>
>    - (b) formally refer the dispute over the correctness of the register
> to the appropriate tribunal/court, making clear that HM Land Registry
> recognises that the identity‑fraud evidence raises a real issue about
> whether the register is accurate.
>
> 4. Confirm that, if it is ultimately determined that the register is
> mistaken and cannot be rectified without prejudice to third parties, HM
> Land Registry will treat me as having a potential claim for indemnity under
> Schedule 8.
>
> Please also confirm any further documents you require (for example, copies
> of the licence, the BP v Buckler pleadings/judgment, and my grandmother’s
> certificates) so that the stage‑two review can consider the identity
> evidence in full.
>
> Fraud unravels all. The limitation act also had a clause for fraud.
> Furthermore any limitation begins from discovery of fraud not occurrence of
> it.
>
> The convenient and timely death of my nan after her two obstructed
> attempts to make her case in 1974, followed by my father's convenient and
> timely death after his appeal of the 1987 case was dismissed and his ECHR
> obstructed, along with our forceful removal by 30 police and bailiffs in
> 1988. And the press reporting us as squatters on our ancestral birthland
> since 1667, did unlawfully dispossess and disposition us, but it doesn't
> change the facts.
>
> I see this case as instrumental in Wales' decolonisation. Whereby us
> indigneous Welsh Nationals on our ancestral birthland are victim to a
> crime. And I am the only one willing to speak up and out as my family of
> mostly women, are all too traumatised by this crime.
>
> It's evident illicit profits and gains. Identity fraud. And negligence and
> incompetence. I absolutely see the Brit-ish Establishment that now occupy
> and rule through force, stealth/ secrecy and licence as terrorists and us
> your hostages. As a direct result of this case.
>
> This is now a hostage terrorist situation on our lands. Well, my family
> are your hostages, I'm more of a counter officer soldier. So put it right.
> I will not stand down.
>
> Regards,
>
> Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sgt)
> Rightful Squire & executor of Manon of Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan, Wales.
>
>
>
>

Buckler 1987. My dad appealed it, it was dismissed. He then sought ECHR,
blocked. He then died. The trauma on our family frightened and immobilised
everyone from seeking justice. Even unto this day.

I found a lot of fraud & concealment in this case. There's also a lot of
media coverage in archives. I wondered if the clause in the limitations act
could allow me to reopen the case on these grounds. The museum confirmed to
be last week all the items exhevated from under our farm after it was
stolen from us.

I'll give you one of the 12 arguments I have where it concerns clauses in
the limitation act to reopen the case. My nan fought off the alleged
possessor, BP Pensions Trust Ltd, for many years - and  maintained
equitable title ownership of our 800 year old farm. But the judge ruled
that BP Properties Ltd, the claimant in the 1987 case, were ignored. And
the BP companies were seperate, so rejecting one doesn't inherently meaning
rejecting the other. And so their letter of offer, a license to stay at
"their" farm until she died, upheld and stopped the clock on adverse
possession. Which was the position of our family (since our title deeds had
gone missing from our home and copy gone from the public library during all
this multi generational lawfare).

But in my dads appeal (point 3/3) he argued BP Pensions Trust should have
been the claimant, not BP Properties Ltd. To which the judges dismissed the
appeal citing - both BP companies are basically the same.

So a blatant case of "Heads they win, tails we lose". Not to mention the
relationship between British Government and BP in those years being a huge
bias.

Furthermore my nan wasn't alive to defend her position in 87. And no
evidence was presented of the alleged letter from BP to stop the clock of
adverse possession. Yet the case was won on the fact a letter of rejection,
from a now dead woman, wasn't able to be presented. It is insane how BP
took possession of our family farm of 400 years of occupancy.

Our farm was prime real estate, overlooking Cardiff bay. This is an Erin
Brokovitch scale scandal. It gets more wild. In my research I discovered
Marconi stayed with us while inventing Radio. My great grandad took him via
horse & cart every day, to Lavenock Point Penarth, to conduct his radio
experiments - including the day of the first successful broadcast. There's
not even a plaque there today to commemorate that Llandough is the
birthplace of radio. I'm also a decorated Royal Signals veteran (honourable
discharge). Just 23 houses built over the site now. CADW expressly rejected
a petition at the time too, which would afford our 800 year old farm
protection from demolishment. Not only was the farm demolished, it was done
during the night and early morning after the lawfare in the court which is
an evident act of  desperation and relentlessness.

My family would like justice. I believe we have a strong case. The
councillor of Llandough is very interested. I just need legal
representation to take this forward.

I look forward to your reply on that matter too if you wouldn't mind. I did
call and leave a message about it last week as well.


Regards,

Sion Buckler

Ms Griffiths,

Thanks for your letter of 23 March 2026 regarding the historic registration
of Ty Mawr Farm, title WA231076. I note your explanation of HM Land
Registry’s administrative role and that you say there is no evidence of a
“mistake” on the basis of the file you have reviewed.

My family’s concern, however, is that the first registration was procured
by misrepresentation and identity fraud by BP, rather than by a simple
clerical error. The occupier was my grandmother, Mrs Williams, from a
family that had occupied the property and land since at least 1667, not the
fictitious “Mrs Buckler” BP fabricated in 1974 for their unilateral
licence, which was the basis of the BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987) case.
BP also appears to have failed to disclose the long‑running ownership
dispute. In a 1978 suppressed newspaper article, my grandmother publicly
asserted her ownership and stated that BP could not prove ownership and had
never obtained a court ruling that it was the owner, only possession orders.

How was BP able to register our land in its name? Did HM Land Registry
enquire whether there was any dispute over the land, given that the dispute
appears in court records from 1974? Twice that year BP obstructed my
grandmother from making her case that she owned the land: first, the
hearing was adjourned without a ruling; then the licence letters, using
identity fraud, prevented the second hearing from taking place. These were
opportunities to dispossess a widowed, disabled woman.
Had HM Land Registry recorded or investigated the existence of this
dispute, BP’s inability to prove ownership, the archaeological and historic
significance of the site, or sought a copy of my grandmother’s death
certificate to see that the name on the licence and narrative were
completely different, we believe BP would not have been able to achieve
first registration on the basis presented. Instead, the use of the wrong
name (“Mrs Buckler” instead of my married grandmother, Mrs Williams) and
the non‑disclosure of the dispute and family claim enabled dispossession
through what we say was identity fraud, which my grandmother was unable to
contest as she also died in the same year as registration.

I wish to append to this land parcel our maintained position of dispute. We
never surrendered. We were removed by around 30 police officers and
information was suppressed. My family being paralysed by fear and silence
is not the same as surrender from sound mind and agency.
Further background is set out at bpvsbuckler.datro.xyz. My family wants
narrative justice as the possibly rightful, dispossessed via fraud,
executors of the Manor of Llandough.

I am aware that HM Land Registry operates a statutory indemnity and redress
scheme under the Land Registration Act 2002, and that substantial payments
(including around £8 million in a single year) have been made where people
suffer loss because of mistakes or fraud in the register. I therefore wish
to explore, formally, whether our family’s loss of Ty Mawr Farm, in
circumstances where BP’s misrepresentations and the suppression of an
active dispute were not reflected on the register, can be considered within
that indemnity/redress framework.

In light of the above, I ask HM Land Registry to state clearly whether you
accept or deny that:
BP was able to obtain first registration of Ty Mawr Farm even though there
was no court ruling that BP owned the land and BP had been unable to prove
ownership in proceedings, which were confined to possession.

The land was registered while there was an active and public dispute over
ownership (including my grandmother’s 1978 public assertion of ownership
and the BP v Buckler litigation), and while the long‑term occupier, my
grandmother, had died and was therefore unable to challenge the application.

My grandmother’s identity and superior family title and land claim
associated with that name were mis‑described in the material on which you
relied, as BP used “Mrs Buckler” instead of my married grandmother’s actual
name, Mrs Williams, and that this misdescription and the concealment of the
dispute were not detected or queried by HM Land Registry before completing
first registration.�
If these matters are admitted, I consider they amount to negligence and
maladministration by HM Land Registry in allowing BP to register our family
land in its name in those circumstances. If you do not accept that, please
explain precisely which of the above points you dispute and on what basis,
so that I can take appropriate legal advice and pursue an indemnity/redress
claim if available.
Separately from that, please also:
Provide official copies of the 23 May 1975 and 19 November 1982
conveyances, and of the first registration applications and all supporting
documents for WA231076 and WA240304, so I can obtain specialist advice on
the extent of any misrepresentation in what was lodged.

Confirm the correct procedure and forms to make a claim under your
indemnity/redress scheme in a historic case of alleged fraud and
misrepresentation in first registration, and whether you consider this
matter potentially falls within that scheme, subject to evidence.

I appreciate that you cannot determine the underlying ownership dispute,
but it is important that HM Land Registry notes that the Buckler/Williams
family contests the integrity of the original registration of Ty Mawr Farm
on the basis of identity fraud, non‑disclosure of a live dispute, and the
absence of any judicial determination that BP owned the land.

Regards,

Sion Buckler

I don't mean to appear litigious, but the other matter I have is BP vs Buckler 1987. My dad appealed it, it was dismissed. He then sought ECHR, blocked. He then died. The trauma on our family frightened and immobilised everyone from seeking justice. Even unto this day.

I found a lot of fraud & concealment in this case. There's also a lot of media coverage in archives. I wondered if the clause in the limitations act could allow me to reopen the case on these grounds. The museum confirmed to be last week all the items exhevated from under our farm after it was stolen from us.

I'll give you one of the 12 arguments I have where it concerns clauses in the limitation act to reopen the case. My nan fought off the alleged possessor, BP Pensions Trust Ltd, for many years - and  maintained equitable title ownership of our 800 year old farm. But the judge ruled that BP Properties Ltd, the claimant in the 1987 case, were ignored. And the BP companies were seperate, so rejecting one doesn't inherently meaning rejecting the other. And so their letter of offer, a license to stay at "their" farm until she died, upheld and stopped the clock on adverse possession. Which was the position of our family (since our title deeds had gone missing from our home and copy gone from the public library during all this multi generational lawfare).

But in my dads appeal (point 3/3) he argued BP Pensions Trust should have been the claimant, not BP Properties Ltd. To which the judges dismissed the appeal citing - both BP companies are basically the same.

So a blatant case of "Heads they win, tails we lose". Not to mention the relationship between British Government and BP in those years being a huge bias.

Furthermore my nan wasn't alive to defend her position in 87. And no evidence was presented of the alleged letter from BP to stop the clock of adverse possession. Yet the case was won on the fact a letter of rejection, from a now dead woman, wasn't able to be presented. It is insane how BP took possession of our family farm of 400 years of occupancy.

Our farm was prime real estate, overlooking Cardiff bay. This is an Erin Brokovitch scale scandal. It gets more wild. In my research I discovered Marconi stayed with us while inventing Radio. My great grandad took him via horse & cart every day, to Lavenock Point Penarth, to conduct his radio experiments - including the day of the first successful broadcast. There's not even a plaque there today to commemorate that Llandough is the birthplace of radio. I'm also a decorated Royal Signals veteran (honourable discharge). Just 23 houses built over the site now. CADW expressly rejected a petition at the time too, which would afford our 800 year old farm protection from demolishment. Not only was the farm demolished, it was done during the night and early morning after the lawfare in the court which is an evident act of  desperation and relentlessness.

My family would like justice. I believe we have a strong case. The councillor of Llandough is very interested. I just need legal representation to take this forward.

I look forward to your reply on that matter too if you wouldn't mind. I did call and leave a message about it last week as well.

From: Sion Buckler
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 19:16 UTC
------------------------------------------------------------

I write on behalf of myself and my siblings, who are the heirs and
successors of Mary Williams of the Williams family, the rightful owners and
occupiers of Great House Farm, Llandough, since 1667 until our unlawful,
unconstitution and inhumane dispossession by armed force in 1988. For which
we remain dispossessed, defrauded and without justice or even narrative
justice, unto this day. The public also lost a site of historic and
archelogical significants and were lied to about what went on. The land
looted too, which is a loss to our nation and people.

I apologise if any of this is incoherent. I am the only member of my family
willing to speak out; the rest, who are nearly all women (sisters, mum,
aunties etc), are petrified of the repercussions, given what happened to
our family in the 1980s. Or dead from this. My father, nan, grandad and
possibly great grandad and maybe more, all potentially murdered.

All this is also chilling in that the playbook used here, could be
industrial scale and nationwide  and have occured to other families too.
Our case might be the foundations for a class action for the public.

dispossession of Great House Farm, Llandough, following the landmark legal
case *BP v Buckler* [1987], which I allege involved:

- **Denial of the right to be heard by the Land Registry.** My grandmother,
Mary Williams (falsely named "Mrs Buckler" on the licence letter produced
by BP in 1974, in order to diminish the Williams ancestral superior land
claim), conveniently died while our family was in mourning during the
limited window granted by the Land Registry to challenge BP's registration
of our land and property in their name in 1982/83. Similarly, my
grandfather died before he was able to clarify—even to my grandmother—how
her fee simple absolute title deed ended up in BP's possession. Until her
dying breath, she maintained her ownership claim, despite repeated unlawful
attempts over decades to dislodge the firm position she held regarding her
and our undisputed ancestral and superior land claim. The official records
and narrative are wrong; there are court errors, suppressed evidence,
procedural unfairness, fraud, and the list goes on.

grandmother held to my father and mother. They never had, nor entered into,
any such agreement with BP. The ruling also alleged that my grandmother
accepted BP's licence letters by non-response, which was untrue. It further
stated that any objection should have been directed to the BP Pension Trust
rather than the claimant, BP Properties, which were deemed separate
companies. Yet in my father's subsequent appeal against the *BP v Buckler*
ruling, his appeal was dismissed on the grounds that the BP companies were
effectively the same—so "heads BP wins, tails we lose." Our 800-year-old
home was then demolished and all money and possessions removed, despite a
court injunction ordering that nothing be removed. My father's ECHR
application was blocked; he was arrested without charge, hospitalised, and
then he conveniently died at the age of 41. Our remaining family,
consisting mostly of women and children, have to this day been too
terrified to speak about this case because of the decades of crimes
committed against our household by the British State. It was synonymous
with a battle or war. I say this as a military warfare professional and
Iraq War veteran: a certified and experienced military commander and
leader. I concluded my military career with honours as an Acting Sergeant.
My profession is cyber and electronic warfare.

from 1988, bailiffs occupied our stolen land and property, and even
dislocated my mother's shoulder for simply serving them a lawful court
injunction. I also question how ITV came to declassify and publish this
footage to YouTube a few months ago, after the months I have spent seeking
information. That did not go unnoticed. There is liability there, and I do
not accept ITV's belief that this quiet release of suppressed news coverage
makes the matter right—though the action is appreciated. How did it come to
be suppressed in the first place? And why is it cut abruptly, at what
appears to be SAS performing a siege on my family home and dislocating my
pregnant mother's shoulder?

Without my discovery of fraud this year—which has taken me two decades, a
career in military cyber and electronic warfare, and recent innovations in
AI to discover and unravel—we had no redress or recourse due to the statute
of limitations and the passage of time, notwithstanding that we were all
too traumatised, like hostages under terrorists, to speak out. We have
received no support to this day for what we were subjected to.

This whole affair, even to this day, represents scandalous treatment of me
and my family. We never surrendered our claim. The manorial titles of the
Manor of Llandough are rightfully ours. The fee simple absolute title has
been ours for over a century, a fact that is also suppressed and withheld
from the defrauded—and implicated—Land Registry.

I am also a war veteran who left my military career with honours and was
employed until 2024 under the Vale of Glamorgan Council / Welsh Government.
I completed my 22 years' service oath *bona fide*. I am an indigenous Welsh
Briton, and this is my ancestral birthland (established 1667). The
disrespect shown by the Vale MP and Llandough Councillor in simply ignoring
me and this matter is abhorrent.

ITV coverage (suppressed until recent months) also reports that neighbours
described the eviction as an "SAS-style operation" to remove us by force in
1988 (myself included). The men in the video do look like SAS. I have
submitted an FOI request to the MOD. Shareholders of mine are SAS, so I
shall find out one way or another, even if I receive an NCND reply. This
matter was also raised in Parliament, who classified and disposed of the
records.

Margaret Thatcher's administration at the time (the British Government) was
evidently assisting BP in clawing assets for the UK Government's sale and
exit at the time, which might explain how 30 police—and possibly SAS—were
used to rip us from our home and land. The human rights violations remain
unanswered.

The Land Registry ultimately had checks and balances lifted and total free
rein during Thatcher's reign, while BP's lawyers evidently committed
perjury in their declarations to the Land Registry, withholding information
from it and supplying it with false information.

All the while, Welsh television was simultaneously interviewing Gaddafi in
Libya in 1988, where he accused Thatcher and the British State of being the
real terrorists, not him. My oath ended in 2024; I am also a Welsh
national. I have no allegiance to the British State. If it acts like my
enemy, it is my enemy. I am absolutely a Welsh national and counter-officer
now that it is so evident the British State waged civil war upon us
indigenous Britons—me and my family included—on our ancestral birthland.

Other media coverage alleged by UK courts to exist from 1974 seems
non-existent or suppressed too. Much is behind paywalls. This whole case
needs to be in the public eye. I have put everyone I can think of on notice.

Fraud and procedural unfairness are ultimately rampant in the case of my
family's dispossession. Aside from all my family members dying at
convenient junctures instrumental in the windows to change the outcome, I
still have major concerns regarding how the MOJ took months to respond only
to fob me off last week; how the MP fobbed me off and will not provide a
proper response; how CADW and Llandough Parish allege this is nothing to do
with them, despite CADW failing to list the farmhouse as Grade II so it
could be demolished (as per a 1,700-signature petition, which was
practically the whole town at the time); the current councillor for
Llandough failing to reply properly; and the fact that the National
Archives report gaps, missing records, and suppressed records.
Notwithstanding that Marconi was staying with us while inventing radio, and
the town will not even put a plaque up to commemorate this, which is
further erasure of the history and known (but suppressed) archaeological
and historic significance of the site. In BP's planning application
records, they state that our 800-year-old former courthouse home was merely
an old, dilapidated building.

Notwithstanding the suppression of the 1870 Roman soldier remains we
discovered when changing our floor from stone to timber, also suppressed to
hide the site's archaeological significance so that housing development
could be unlawfully approved. BP did not even seek a ruling on ownership;
they only sought possession, most likely so that the discovery and
significance of the site's archaeology could be pretended not to be known
until the excavation of our land in 1994—which is further evidence of
blatant conspiracy and fraud.

These are the actions of a crime or terrorist network, seeking to install a
terrorist cell or camp. It is worse than simply the British colonising
Wales.

Notwithstanding the child graves secretly moved from the church next door
during the excavation, which seemed to take ten years to be properly
reported on, and even then their numbers in the report appear to be
underrepresented.

The scandal continues endlessly. There are court errors too. The fancy
Latin words diminish and falsely describe my grandmother's land claim and
superior ownership (it was "older than man can remember," not merely a
"claim to the land"). The language used by the court clearly demonstrates
bias prior to the ruling—language implying that my late grandmother, Mrs
Williams (*not* Mrs Buckler, as they falsely named her in document fraud),
was imagining her ancestral superior land claim, in order to discredit her
through carefully selected judicial wording.

My siblings and I remain the heirs and successors and landowners. Nothing
has lawfully broken or undone that claim. We demand that the fraud,
corruption, gaps in records, false records, and myriad crimes committed
against us be addressed and not ignored. There should be a Senedd public
inquiry into this. My family should not be dispossessed a second longer. We
are seriously looking at £100 million in reparations if the truth of this
matter becomes known, given the scale of the scandal and injustice.

In 1667 we acquired the land and property in a 999-year lease (virtual
freehold). In the early 1900s we obtained the superior paper title—free and
clear, outright equitable ownership—via the deal with Bute Estate quarryman
Daniel Thomas, which led to the tree-planting ceremony to affirm this in
history. *(See attached.)*

Frederick Buckler's transfer of Mrs Williams's equitable title to BP and
their predecessors, without her knowledge or consent, is not legitimate and
should never have stood, nor does it stand to reason. His inability to
clarify the details of the alleged transaction due to his convenient death
afterwards does not make it right, as Mary Williams maintained her position
after his death. It was never his title to sell, even if he did. My
grandmother was left unable to prove her standing, and the 1974 hearing was
adjourned. The dismissal of the second hearings in 1974 due to the licence
letter issued by BP (resorting to identity and document fraud) does not
negate the fact that there was never a ruling stating BP owned our land,
despite their purchasing my grandmother's stolen fee simple absolute title
deed. BP only ever sought possession. They could not obtain a ruling
because it would have meant discovery, unveiling the archaeological
significance that would have prevented land and housing development.

This was a coordinated campaign of fraud, stealth, and administrative
erasure spanning decades, employing force, secrecy, and fraudulent licence.
By hook and by crook we were dispossessed of our land. Thatcher—and
potentially the SAS—make it, at the least, an allodial/eminent domain
seizure, in which case we should still be due compensation.

I fail to see the proclaimed authority of the other men on my land,
alleging themselves to be a government and citizens rather than terrorists,
who both ostracised and held my family hostage, if legitimacy does not
exist. You need legitimacy to claim authority.

**Summary of the Fraudulent Dispossession:**

**The Title Theft:** Evidence supports that a "Title-for-Quarrying"
agreement existed with Daniel Thomas of the Bute Estate. We obtained this
fee simple absolute title lawfully, but it was later secretly and
fraudulently taken and sold back to Bute / Western Ground Rents / BP
without the knowledge or consent of the rightful owner, Mary Williams.
Parliament even stated on record how criminal Western Ground Rents were.

**Procedural Fraud (The 1974 Licence):** The 1987 Court of Appeal ruling
was predicated on a unilateral "licence letter" issued by the landlords'
solicitors. We reject this ruling. It should be set aside on grounds of
fraud.

**Identity Erasure:** Throughout all legal proceedings, Mary Williams was
intentionally misidentified as "Mrs Buckler." This was a calculated tactic
to strip her of her ancestral "Williams" lineage and the superior land
rights and claim associated with it.

**Exploitation of Mortality:**
- **Frederick Buckler:** Died before the circumstances of how Mary was
dispossessed of her title—and how the other parties regained possession
after the lawful Daniel Thomas (and/or Anthony Williams) dealings with Bute
Estate—could be clarified. This is inconsequential, much like Mary's own
death; neither changed her position on the matter, which she did voice,
despite what the 1987 ruling falsely alleges.
- **Mary Williams:** Died during the precise two-week window required to
rebut the Land Registry's registration of the land in BP's name—a window we
believe was exploited to finalise this theft. At minimum, this is the case;
it is more likely she was murdered. Her husband before her too. And my
father, William Buckler, given the convenient timing of all their
deaths—not to mention the unfair dismissal of my father's appeal, the
blocking of his ECHR request, the theft and demolition of his property and
our home prior to his death.

**Our Position:**
The Williams family (now the Buckler family) has never ceased our claim. We
maintain that the land was taken through criminal stealth and that the
current registered titles are poisoned by this original fraud. We seek full
reparations for the loss of ancestral wealth, the destruction of the Roman
archaeological site on the property, and the systematic denial of our right
to a fair trial.

Please provide a formal response and update regarding your position on this
matter within 14 days. Please also hold to account those taking steps back
into the shadows, as this only makes the matter more clandestine and
therefore makes me very jumpy as a military warfare professional. I already
fly in and out as if on another tour of the Middle East, and my family
remain hostages under terrorists.

I would also ask that Companies House, who have recently tried to
criminalise me, give me some space. They gave me three options to submit
ID: a questionnaire with passport and driving licence (which I provided);
Post Office verification; or Digital ID. I chose the first option. They
will not accept it. But I will not be lured to a location of their
choosing, nor will I put any of their tracking ID applications on my
devices. I do not trust the regime on that island. Until this and another
unnamed matter of similar scale is resolved, I consider the British
Government a terrorist organisation and do not recognise its authority. My
family there are hostages under said terrorists. And Church View Close,
Llandough—23 houses—is a terrorist cell/camp on my land.

Marconi was staying with us in Llandough when he invented radio. This too
was covered up. Cardiff City will not put a plaque naming Marconi as the
inventor on the statue of a radio at Cardiff Bay—not even a plaque to
commemorate it. Llandough should be a tourist attraction based on this fact
alone, rather than the occupying terrorist network's cell of 23 houses, as
I see it.

Regards,

**Sion Buckler Esq.** (Ret'd Sgt)
On behalf of and as one of the Heirs and Successors of Mary Williams, Great
House Farm, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan

of Glamorgan Council). I now write in a private capacity, not under oath,
and not in any adversarial posture, but in good faith and with the
intention that the historic record be accurately preserved.

My purpose in writing is to place on record serious concerns regarding the
historical treatment, documentation, and subsequent erasure of my family’s
ancestral estate, Tŷ Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough, in the Vale of
Glamorgan.

Tŷ Mawr was an historic monastic grange and site of Roman antiquity. From
1667, it was held in continuous occupation and stewardship by my fathers
sides maternal family, the Williams family, later intersecting with the
Buckler line through marriage. For over three centuries, my forebears
occupied, worked, and maintained this land. I was born there.

Prior to enlisting in Signals Intelligence roles and encountering senior
national and royal figures in the course of official duties, I was educated
in Wales, including at Llandovery College, which I attended under the
Government-run Assisted Places Scheme, having been selected on academic
merit. On my mothers side, my late grandfather, the Welsh BAFTA-winning
actor Ray Smith, carried the same Welsh cultural identity into public life.
My wider family has likewise contributed to Welsh cultural life, including
my aunt Shan Cothi, the opera singer, and her husband/ my late uncle;
Justin Smith, founder of the Welsh band Tigertailz and directed a major
'visit wales' campaign for the tourist board. These details are to
demonstrate continuity of Welsh cultural life rooted in this family and
place. I'm also a fluent speak Welsh, I named my daugher Delyth, and I do
much for the continuity of Welsh cultural life.

In 1974, my grandmother on my fathers side; Mary Williams, initiated
proceedings concerning the title to Tŷ Mawr. Those proceedings were
adjourned and later that same year effectively extinguished without
substantive resolution. Critically, my grandmother never adopted her
husband’s surname; she remained Mary Williams throughout her life. That
name was not incidental. It was the living link to the 1667 acquisition of
the farm and to our family’s long occupation.

During later proceedings, the name “Mrs Buckler” was ascribed to her in
court records. This misidentification had material consequences. It severed
the documentary continuity of the Williams line and undermined both our de
facto occupation and any consideration of adverse possession. This
misnaming remains, to my knowledge, uncorrected in the public record.

In 1988, my family was forcibly removed from Tŷ Mawr, having been
characterised as squatters despite centuries of occupation. Our home — an
800-year-old farmhouse — was demolished shortly thereafter. I was four
years old. I witnessed the destruction alongside my siblings and parents.
We were not permitted to retrieve belongings or family records. Centuries
of family material history were lost.

Of particular concern is that the site had long been associated with Roman
remains. In 1870, a Roman burial was reportedly uncovered on the land, a
fact later omitted or minimised in official descriptions of the site.
Following the demolition of the farmhouse, and prior to residential
development, it emerged that the land contained what is now understood to
be the largest Roman burial site excavated in Wales, with over 1,000
burials. Had this been properly recorded and acknowledged earlier,
statutory archaeological protections should have applied.

The effect of these events has been the near-total erasure of the historic
and indigenous Welsh continuity of Tŷ Mawr from public narrative and
record. The land now forms part of a modern housing development, without
acknowledgment of its significance or of the family that occupied it for
over three centuries.

I wish to be clear: my primary concern is not confrontation, but correction
— correction of the historical record, acknowledgment of documented
irregularities, and preservation of truth for future generations. My family
has carried the consequences of these events for decades, including
significant trauma, and many remain reluctant to come forward.

I hold a forensic analysis estimating the financial losses associated with
Tŷ Mawr at approximately £101.2 million, but the greater matter is not
monetary. It is the restoration of narrative accuracy and the
acknowledgment of indigenous Welsh continuity at this site and my families
standing in our local community thereafter. The generational trauma is so
deep, even last week my mother refused to discuss this, even privately.

I do not write to demand action from His Majesty personally, nor do I
presume upon the Crown. I write so that it cannot later be said that these
matters were unknown or unrecorded. I respectfully request that this
correspondence be retained as a notice of concern regarding historic record
integrity, misidentification of parties, and the suppression or omission of
material archaeological and cultural facts.

My intention is also to rebuild an exact replica of Great House Farm in
Patagonia, where the Welsh community here has welcomed the preservation of
this history. This project is intended as an act of cultural conservation,
not protest.

I remain respectful of the Crown’s constitutional role and of the King
personally. My request is simply that the truth of Tŷ Mawr — its history,
its people, and its erasure — is not allowed to disappear entirely from the
historical record.

I certify that I write in good faith, with full mental capacity, and
without hostility. I seek only truth, acknowledgment, and preservation of
history.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Hywel Buckler
[redacted], Wales

Subject: Subject: Stage Two Complaint – Title WA231076 – Alleged Mistake in the Register
From: Sion Buckler
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 19:29 UTC
------------------------------------------------------------

Sir or Madam,

I write to ask that my complaint regarding title number WA231076 (Land on
the North Side of Leckwith Road, Llandough) be escalated to **stage two**
of HM Land Registry’s Complaints Procedure. This email sets out why I
consider the stage‑one decision to be incorrect, identifies the mistake I
say exists in the register, and explains the decision I seek.

### 1. My core contention

My core contention is that BP Properties Limited were registered as
proprietors on the basis of a factual and legal error regarding my
grandmother’s status on the land. My grandmother did not occupy under any
genuine licence granted to her and did not relinquish any claim. Instead,
any licence relied on by BP related to a different name/person. As her
heir, I have succeeded to her claim; I therefore say that registering BP as
proprietors was a “mistake in the register” for the purposes of the Land
Registration Act 2002.

### 2. Identity mismatch and alleged “licence”

Your stage‑one letter records that HM Land Registry relies on the Court of
Appeal decision in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler  EWCA Civ 2, and treats my
grandmother as having occupied under a licence granted by the documentary
title holder, so that her possession was no longer adverse.

However, the alleged licence and related correspondence did not use my
grandmother’s true legal name. My grandmother was Mrs Williams (supported
by her birth, marriage and death certificates), not “Mrs Buckler”. The
“licensee” referred to in BP’s narrative and in the 1987 litigation is
therefore not the same legal person as my grandmother. There is, in other
words, a fundamental mis‑identification or identity fraud at the heart of
the story that HM Land Registry and the Court have relied upon.

If the licence relied on by BP was addressed to, or granted in respect of,
a different named individual, it cannot properly be said that my
grandmother’s occupation was under that licence. In that case her
occupation remained adverse to BP’s paper title, and any finding that she
was a “licensee” rests on a factual premise that is demonstrably wrong.

### 3. Timing – “cart before the horse”

Your letter explains that the applications for first registration of
WA231076 (and the related title WA240304) were made in 1982–83 and that BP
demonstrated a documentary root of title back to 1969/1975 by way of
conveyances and a 1971 abstract of title.

You also confirm that the Court of Appeal only gave its decision in BP
Properties Ltd v Buckler in 1987, holding that an offer by BP to let my
grandmother remain created a licence and brought her adverse possession to
an end.

This highlights a fundamental sequencing problem:

- At the date of first registration (1982–83), whether there was a valid
licence capable of defeating my grandmother’s adverse possession was a
live, unresolved dispute.
- BP nevertheless presented themselves as entitled to be registered as
proprietors and their solicitors certified on form FR1 that there was no
question or doubt affecting the title.

- HM Land Registry, relying on that certification, registered BP before any
court had determined whether my grandmother’s possession had extinguished
BP’s title.
- Only in 1987 did the Court of Appeal retrospectively treat the alleged
licence as bringing adverse possession to an end, and that decision was
itself based on the mis‑identification described above.

In simple terms, the effect of the alleged licence (if any) was judicially
determined **after** first registration, and on the basis of the wrong
person being treated as the “licensee”. BP and their solicitors put the
cart before the horse, and HM Land Registry accepted that position.

### 4. The specific “mistake in the register”

Your stage‑one response concludes that there is “no evidence of a mistake
in the register” and therefore no power to alter the register and no right
to indemnity. I say this is incorrect.

The mistake I allege is as follows:

1. On the true facts, my grandmother’s occupation of the land was adverse
to BP’s documentary title and was not under any valid licence granted to
her.

2. Her adverse possession had, or may have, extinguished BP’s title by the
time of first registration in 1982–83, meaning BP were not entitled to be
registered as proprietors at that time.

3. HM Land Registry nevertheless registered BP as proprietors on the basis
of:
   - a licence attributed to the wrong person (identity error/fraud), and
   - a solicitor’s FR1 certificate stating there was no question or doubt
affecting title, despite a long‑running dispute and pending litigation.

4. Subsequent reliance on the 1987 Court of Appeal decision does not cure
this, because that decision itself proceeded on the mis‑identification of
my grandmother and did not and could not retrospectively validate a licence
that never related to her.

On that analysis, the register shows BP as proprietors when, in law, my
grandmother’s adverse possession should have extinguished BP’s title and
given rise to a transmissible proprietary interest which I, as her heir,
now claim. The register therefore does not accurately reflect the true
legal position and contains a mistake capable of rectification.

### 5. Why the stage‑one reasoning is inadequate

In your stage‑one letter you state that:

- HM Land Registry has an administrative function and cannot “look behind
or challenge decisions of the Court”. [1]
- My identity‑fraud claims are “not relevant to the issue of title to the
land” because they relate to the dispute heard by the Court.

- There is no evidence of negligence or maladministration and no evidence
of a mistake in the register.

With respect, this reasoning is incomplete:

- Once HM Land Registry is presented with clear evidence that the person
named as the “licensee” in the litigation and licence documentation is not
the same legal person as the occupier (my grandmother), that goes directly
to whether the Court of Appeal’s factual premise remains reliable and
whether the register is accurate.

- Recognising that there is a serious question as to the correctness of the
register is not the same as “overturning” the Court of Appeal. HM Land
Registry has statutory powers to alter the register where there is a
mistake, and it can, where appropriate, refer disputes about rectification
to the tribunal or the courts.

- To simply say that identity‑fraud concerns are “not relevant to title”
is, I say, an error of law and/or an unreasonable application of policy. It
disregards new evidence going to the foundation of BP’s claimed entitlement.

### 6. The decision and outcome I seek

For stage two, I ask that a Land Registrar (Senior Officer) reconsider the
complaint and:

1. Accept that the combination of:
   - the identity mismatch (licence/name vs my grandmother’s true legal
name), and
   - the timing (registration in 1982–83 before the 1987 decision) gives
rise to at least a **serious question** as to whether the register is
mistaken in showing BP/ Companies thereafter, as proprietors.

2. Treat this as evidence of a potential “mistake in the register” for the
purposes of your alteration powers and Schedule 8, rather than as a mere
disagreement with the 1987 judgment.

3. Either:

   - (a) commence the process of rectification, recognising that my
grandmother’s adverse possession may have extinguished BP’s title and that
I, as her heir, now have a claim to be registered, or

   - (b) formally refer the dispute over the correctness of the register to
the appropriate tribunal/court, making clear that HM Land Registry
recognises that the identity‑fraud evidence raises a real issue about
whether the register is accurate.

4. Confirm that, if it is ultimately determined that the register is
mistaken and cannot be rectified without prejudice to third parties, HM
Land Registry will treat me as having a potential claim for indemnity under
Schedule 8.

Please also confirm any further documents you require (for example, copies
of the licence, the BP v Buckler pleadings/judgment, and my grandmother’s
certificates) so that the stage‑two review can consider the identity
evidence in full.

Fraud unravels all. The limitation act also had a clause for fraud.
Furthermore any limitation begins from discovery of fraud not occurrence of
it.

The convenient and timely death of my nan after her two obstructed attempts
to make her case in 1974, followed by my father's convenient and timely

I see this case as instrumental in Wales' decolonisation. Whereby us

It's evident illicit profits and gains. Identity fraud. And negligence and
incompetence. I absolutely see the Brit-ish Establishment that now occupy

This is now a hostage terrorist situation on our lands. Well, my family are

Regards,

Sion Buckler Esq. (Ret'd Sgt)
